aria: Animated recap of the Cavaliers' 126 to 115 home win over the Bulls: Donovan Mitchell's running layup with 1:13 left that put Cleveland back up 10, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Mitchell's season-high 39 points, the top scorers, how the Cavaliers won, and the next game against Memphis.
notes: Box score from the Cavaliers' 126–115 win over the Chicago Bulls at Rocket Arena in Cleveland on Nov 16, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via Yahoo Sports), Field Level Media, Cleveland.com (via Yahoo Sports), the Akron Beacon Journal, the Chicago Sun-Times, OnTap Sports Net, ClutchPoints and SI.com. All 126 Cleveland points and all 115 Chicago points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: Chicago led 31–25 after one, Cleveland led 57–48 at the half and 88–79 after three. Team totals (field goals 51 of 97 to 41 of 90, threes 10 of 33 to 12 of 44, free throws 14 of 21 to 21 of 28, rebounds 51–37, offensive rebounds 15–11, assists 33–30) are from the Covers box score; points in the paint (68–50) are from Covers and OnTap Sports Net. Cleveland's biggest lead, 17, came at 68–51 with 9:39 left in the third quarter (OnTap Sports Net; Field Level Media; Covers). Chicago's biggest lead was 8, at 36–28 in the second quarter (Covers). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Monday's games.

Cleveland closed the first half on a 25–10 run and took the lead for good with 5:35 left in the second quarter (OnTap Sports Net; Cleveland.com). Donovan Mitchell scored a season-high 39 on 16 of 25 shooting (Covers; Cleveland.com; Field Level Media), including 20 in the fourth quarter on 8-of-8 shooting (Chicago Sun-Times; OnTap Sports Net). Chicago pulled within 119–113 with 1:39 left on back-to-back baskets by Norman Powell (Field Level Media; OnTap Sports Net). It was Cleveland's second straight win (AP). Evan Mobley missed a third straight game with a toe sprain (Cleveland.com; AP). The Cavaliers host Memphis on Wednesday, Nov 18, at 7 p.m. ET (Cleveland.com; AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Donovan Mitchell's running layup with 1:13 left that pushed the lead back to 10 (Chicago Sun-Times: "hitting a running layup to extend the lead back to 10 with 1:13 left"), right after Jarrett Allen's dunk with 1:27 left made it an 8-point game (Chicago Sun-Times; OnTap Sports Net: "Harden found Jarrett Allen for a dunk on the next trip, and Mitchell's layup ended it"). Field Level Media describes the finish as Mitchell scoring four straight points. The drive is drawn with the template's short pull-up motion finishing at the rim. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Cleveland Cavaliers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Mitchell's listed 6-foot-2 and 215 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with his arms scaled to the 6-foot-10 wingspan from his 2017 draft measurements (Tankathon), in the Cavaliers' home white with No. 45 (Basketball-Reference). His look is from the site's look sheet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
